docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
TRumut is an alignment-free tandem repeat caller for long reads.

  • Please refer to our preprint for why we built TRumut, how it works, and what it finds.
  • Source code is available on GitHub.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Main workflow:

Run trumut allele on each sample. Then, take its output as the input to trumut cancer, trio, or use-pon.

  • trumut cancer: reports alleles in a tumor that are absent from its matched normal
  • trumut trio: reports alleles in a child that are absent from both parents
  • trumut use-pon: reports alleles outside the range seen in a panel of normals. Use it when there is no matched sample to compare against: a tumor without a matched normal, or a single tissue sample screened for mosaic variants

Not needed for the main workflow:

Usage and output details for these three are under Advanced info.

  • trumut prep-catalog: builds a uniqmer catalog for trumut allele from your own tandem repeat catalog  → ready-made version of the catalog available under Pre-built files
  • trumut build-pon: builds a panel of normals for trumut use-pon from your own samples  → ready-made version of the panel available under Pre-built files
  • trumut mutual: compares two or more samples symmetrically, reporting alleles present in one sample but absent from another. The manuscript uses it to profile HiFi error rates

docs.title: Install
docs.text: TRumut can be installed through Bioconda or built from source.

docs.title: Conda install
docs.text:
conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda trumut

The conda package also installs samtools. Other tools that are required for certain inputs are listed under External programs.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • A C++17 compiler: GCC 8+, Clang 7+, or Apple Clang (Xcode 11+)
  • zlib, with development headers (zlib1g-dev on Debian/Ubuntu, zlib-devel on RHEL/Fedora, included with Xcode on macOS)
  • GNU make
  • Linux or macOS (Windows through WSL)
git clone https://github.com/erkim11/trumut.git
cd trumut
make

Then follow the Quick start to check that it runs.

docs.title: External programs
docs.text:
These must be on your PATH, but only for the inputs listed. None is required to build trumut or to run it on local SAM, BAM, FASTA, or FASTQ files.

Tool Needed for samtools CRAM input, alignments streamed from a URL (s3://, https://, gs://, ...) curl FASTA/FASTQ fetched over http, https, or ftp aws CLI FASTA/FASTQ fetched from s3:// gcloud FASTA/FASTQ fetched from gs:// gzip trumut allele output whose file name ends in .gz

docs.title: Pre-built files
docs.text: All files below are in the following Zenodo record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22903449.

docs.title: Downloading
docs.text:
Download from the record page in a browser or from the command line with wget or curl using the file links on that page:

docs.title: Uniqmer-annotated tandem repeat catalog
docs.text:
hg38.trf-b7-b7-p500.uniqmers.tsv

The catalog trumut allele reads, made by trumut prep-catalog from a genome-wide tandem repeat catalog.

Column Description chr chromosome tr_start repeat start (0-based) tr_end repeat end tr_motif repeat motif kmerA_ref_coords, kmerB_ref_coords 0-based reference coordinate of the two uniqmers kmerA_id, kmerB_id uniqmer IDs kmerA_seq, kmerB_seq the 31-mer sequence as the reference lists it kmerA_strand, kmerB_strand reference strand of each uniqmer (+/-)

docs.title: Panel of normals
docs.text:
HPRC.pon.09012026.tsv

The panel trumut use-pon compares against, made by trumut build-pon from normal samples. One row per uniqmer pair.

Column Description chr chromosome kmerA_id, kmerB_id uniqmer IDs range_min, range_max smallest / largest allele length seen in the panel. NA when too few samples cover the pair range_min_n_motif_kmers, range_max_n_motif_kmers median number of motif k-mers* across samples at that length. NA when unavailable

* An approximate measure of how much of the allele is made of the repeat motif.

docs.title: Inputs for building your own catalog
docs.text: Needed only if you decide to use your own tandem repeat list with trumut prep-catalog instead of using the pre-built catalog above.

docs.title: GRCh38 uniqmers
docs.text:
hs38.ukm579.s02.sorted.txt.gz

Every 31-mer that is conserved and unique in GRCh38 (i.e., uniqmer), with its position. Passed to trumut prep-catalog -k

Column Description chr chromosome position 0-based reference coordinate of the 31-mer kmer_id uniqmer ID: a, x, or y followed by numbers, for autosomes, chrX, and chrY strand reference strand, + or -

docs.title: Uniqmer ID to sequence map
docs.text:
ukm579.s02.txt.gz

The sequence behind each uniqmer ID. Passed to trumut prep-catalog -s.

Column Description kmer_id uniqmer ID, as in the uniqmers file kmer_seq the 31-mer sequence as the reference lists it

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Here we have a test run with small simulated samples so you can try trumut before using your own data. Follow the steps below to confirm everything runs.

docs.title: Get the data
docs.text:
First, download the test data. It lives in the test folder of the TRumut GitHub repository: https://github.com/erkim11/trumut

# run this
git clone https://github.com/erkim11/trumut.git
cd trumut/test

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Warning

If you built TRumut from source, use ../trumut in place of trumut in commands below.

# call tandem repeat alleles in each sample
trumut allele test_reads1.bam test_tr_catalog.tsv.gz reads1.alleles.tsv --input-type reads
trumut allele test_reads2.bam test_tr_catalog.tsv.gz reads2.alleles.tsv --input-type reads
trumut allele test_reads3.bam test_tr_catalog.tsv.gz reads3.alleles.tsv --input-type reads

# cancer: sample 3 plays the tumor, sample 1 its matched normal
trumut cancer reads3.alleles.tsv reads1.alleles.tsv output_cancer.tsv --input-type reads

# trio: sample 3 plays the child, samples 1 and 2 the parents
trumut trio reads3.alleles.tsv reads1.alleles.tsv reads2.alleles.tsv output_trio.tsv --input-type reads

# use-pon: sample 1 against a small panel of normals
trumut use-pon reads1.alleles.tsv test_pon.tsv output_pon.tsv --input-type reads

Each command should finish in seconds.

docs.title: Other input types
docs.text:
The same catalog works with unaligned reads and assemblies:

trumut allele test_reads1.fa.gz test_tr_catalog.tsv.gz reads1.fa.alleles.tsv --input-type reads
trumut allele test_assembly1.fa test_tr_catalog.tsv.gz asm1.alleles.tsv --input-type assembly --ploidy 2

Both give 29 lines.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: For your own data, see Usage for each command and Pre-built files for the genome-wide catalog and panel of normals.

docs.title: Basic command
docs.text:
trumut build-pon [alleles_dir/] [pon.tsv] --input-type reads
trumut build-pon [alleles_dir/] [pon.tsv] --input-type assembly --ploidy 2
  • [alleles_dir/]: directory holding one trumut allele output per normal sample, named *.alleles.tsv
  • [pon.tsv]: output path of the panel of normals
  • --input-type reads|assembly: reads for sequencing reads. assembly for assembled contigs
  • --ploidy N: required with assembly. Number of haplotype contigs per locus (e.g., 1 for a haploid assembly, 2 for diploid)

docs.title: With digests
docs.text:
Digesting each allele output first is optional. A digest is much smaller in file size and merges to an identical panel, so it pays off when the allele outputs live on slow storage or the panel is rebuilt often.

trumut build-pon --digest sample1.alleles.tsv sample1.pon-digest.tsv   # one sample
trumut build-pon --digest alleles_dir/   # every *.alleles.tsv in the directory

# merge as before
trumut build-pon alleles_dir/ pon.tsv --input-type reads
  • sample1.pon-digest.tsv: one digest per sample, written next to the allele output or into an optional output directory given as a third argument
  • the merge uses a sample's digest when one exists and falls back to the raw allele output otherwise

docs.title: More options
docs.text: Argument Default Description --pair-percent-support F 0.98 fraction of ALL samples that must cover a pair for it to be kept --distance-percent-support F 0.0975 fraction of the COVERING samples that must carry a length for it to count as supported --min-reads-per-sample N 10; for assemblies, set by --ploidy a sample "covers" a pair only with at least N reads/contigs there --suffix S .alleles.tsv input filename suffix --jobs J 3 merge tasks at once, or files digested at once in --digest directory mode --split-factor N by chromosome size cut every chromosome into exactly N kmerA_id sub-slices for parallelization --digest off reduces raw outputs to smaller digests that merge to the same panel

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text:
Panel table

Column Present when Description chr, kmerA_id, kmerB_id copied from the trumut allele output range_min, range_max smallest / largest allele length carried by at least --distance-percent-support of the covering samples range_min_n_motif_kmers, range_max_n_motif_kmers median across samples of each sample's median number of motif k-mers* at that length

Digest (--digest)

Column Present when Description chr, kmerA_id, kmerB_id copied from the trumut allele output n_reads number of distinct reads at the pair in that sample allele_lengths distinct allele lengths (list); unlike the allele output, one item per distinct length, not per read motif_kmers median number of motif k-mers* per allele length (list)

* An approximate measure of how much of the allele is made of the repeat motif.

Columns marked (list) hold one comma-separated item per read, in the same order across columns.

docs.title: Basic command
docs.text:
trumut mutual [output.tsv] -i [sample1.tsv] -i [sample2.tsv] ...
  • [output.tsv]: output path
  • -i: trumut allele output. At least two must be given

docs.title: More options
docs.text: Argument Default Description -t chr1 all process specified chromosome only, spelled as in the trumut allele output -j N 3 chromosomes processed in parallel --clustering-thres N 3 allele lengths within N bp of each other collapse into one reported allele --n-reads-thres N = clustering width a read supports an allele if its length is within N bp of it --min-offset N clustering width + 1 report a length only if it is at least N bp from every other input's lengths --min-reads-per-sample N 10 skip a locus unless each sample has at least N reads there --summary path none write a two-section summary: row counts per test sample and reference set (directional), and allele counts per present/absent sample combination (venn)

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text: Column Present when Description chr, region_start, region_end, kmerA_id, kmerB_id, loci copied from the trumut allele output test label (file basename) of the input the allele was found in allele_length allele length in the test sample n_reads number of test sample reads at exactly allele_length n_reads_in_thres number of test sample reads supporting the allele_length (within --n-reads-thres of allele_length) n_refs_deviating number of other samples that lack the allele refs_deviating comma-separated labels of the samples that lack the allele offset_<sample> (one column per input) allele_length minus that sample's nearest allele length. . if the sample carries the allele. NA in the test sample's own column

docs.title: Example output
docs.text:
chr region_start region_end kmerA_id kmerB_id loci test allele_length n_reads n_reads_in_thres n_refs_deviating refs_deviating offset_s1.tsv offset_s2.tsv offset_s3.tsv chr1 3074876 3074933 a482910377 a2918360054 3074876-3074933:CAG s1.tsv 107 14 16 2 s2.tsv,s3.tsv NA 18 21 chr1 9210440 9210476 a730155829 a1604472913 9210440-9210476:TTTA s2.tsv 55 9 11 1 s3.tsv . NA -8 chr2 1188020 1188110 a1049382267 a377258106 1188020-1188061:AT,1188070-1188110:GT s3.tsv 133 12 12 2 s1.tsv,s2.tsv 12 12 NA

Summary file

Directional counts output rows, grouped by the test sample and the set of samples it deviates from. The row with test = s1.tsv and refs_deviating = s3.tsv is exactly what trumut cancer s1.tsv s3.tsv would report. Because every row has one test sample, an allele shared by s1 and s2 but absent from s3 appears twice: once with s1 as test and once with s2 as test.

section test refs_deviating n_rows n_loci directional s1.tsv s3.tsv 158 150 directional s2.tsv s3.tsv 154 147 directional s1.tsv s2.tsv,s3.tsv 265 251

Venn counts alleles, grouped by which samples carry them (present) and which lack them (absent). It merges the output rows to count deviating events detected per sample combination. Each row is one region of a Venn diagram of the samples.

section present absent n_events n_loci venn s1.tsv,s2.tsv s3.tsv 146 139 venn s1.tsv s2.tsv,s3.tsv 251 240 venn s2.tsv,s3.tsv s1.tsv 172 163

docs.title: Basic command
docs.text:
trumut prep-catalog -i [tr_catalog.tsv] -k [uniqmers.tsv.gz] -s [uniqmer_seqs.tsv.gz] -o [catalog.tsv]
  • -i: your tandem repeat catalog, a TSV with a header naming chr, tr_start, tr_end, and tr_motif. Any other columns are carried through
  • -k: uniqmer positions in the reference genome, from Pre-built files
  • -s: uniqmer ID to sequence map, from Pre-built files
  • -o: output path of the uniqmer-annotated catalog, ready for trumut allele

docs.title: More options
docs.text: Argument Default Description -t STR all process specified chromosome only. "1" and "chr1" both match -j N 3 chromosomes processed in parallel --max-repeat-span N 15000 drop catalog rows whose repeat spans more than N bp

docs.title: Input catalog
docs.text: Column Description chr chromosome. 1 and chr1 are treated alike tr_start repeat start (0-based) tr_end repeat end tr_motif repeat motif, or several separated by commas (e.g. TAACCC,AACCCC). A, C, G, T only

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text:
Column Present when Description input columns every column of the input catalog, unchanged and in input order kmerA_ref_coords, kmerB_ref_coords 0-based reference coordinate of the two uniqmers kmerA_id, kmerB_id uniqmer IDs from the -k file kmerA_seq, kmerB_seq the 31-mer sequence as the reference lists it kmerA_strand, kmerB_strand reference strand of each uniqmer (+/-)

A repeat group at a chromosome edge has empty coordinates, ID and strand and NA sequence on the missing side. trumut allele skips such rows.

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text:
Column Present when Description chr chromosome of the uniqmer pair region_start leftmost repeat start coordinate between the two uniqmers (0-based) region_end rightmost repeat end coordinate between the two uniqmers loci catalog tandem repeats between the two uniqmers, as start-end:motif query_names --save-query-names read name, or contig name for assemblies (list) kmerA_id, kmerB_id the two uniqmer IDs kmerA_ref_coords, kmerB_ref_coords --save-kmer-coords reference start of each uniqmer (0-based) n_reads number of reads (or contigs) in which both uniqmers were found allele_lengths number of bases between the two uniqmers (list) n_motif_kmers number of k-mers in the allele sequence that match the repeat motif* (list) allele_seqs --save-allele-seq sequence between the two uniqmers (list) HP haplotype tag, 1 or 2 (list); . if untagged PS phase set (list); . whenever HP is .

* An approximate measure of how much of the allele is made of the repeat motif.

Columns with an empty "Present when" cell are always written. Columns marked (list) hold one comma-separated item per read, in the same order across columns. . marks a missing value.

docs.title: Optional output files
docs.text: Three optional files record what did not make it into the main output. Each is written only when its flag is given.

docs.title: -w, --wrong-kmer-hits
docs.text:
Reads / contigs in which both uniqmers were found once, but on mismatched strands or in the wrong order, so the length between them is not trusted. Same columns as the main output.

chr region_start region_end loci kmerA_id kmerB_id n_reads allele_lengths n_motif_kmers HP PS chr1 3074876 3074933 3074876-3074933:CAG a482910377 a2918360054 2 89,89 51,51 1,. 3050112,. chr5 146878727 146878759 146878727-146878759:CTG a1520497731 a44062815 1 71 26 2 146850990 chr11 2884420 2884480 2884420-2884480:GGA a2231705644 a985170328 3 78,78,81 54,54,57 .,.,. .,.,.

docs.title: -m, --many-kmer-hits
docs.text:
Uniqmer pairs that were found more than once in a single read / contig, so no single length could be measured. The columns depend on the input type.

Reads input: one row per read and pair.

Column Description query_name read name chr, region_start, region_end the pair's region, from the catalog kmerA_id, kmerB_id the two uniqmer IDs kmerA_hit_count, kmerB_hit_count times each uniqmer was found in the read query_name chr region_start region_end kmerA_id kmerB_id kmerA_hit_count kmerB_hit_count m84011/2731/ccs chr1 3074876 3074933 a482910377 a2918360054 2 1 m84011/5108/ccs chr8 118371245 118371301 a1806613252 a3149920067 1 3 m84011/6620/ccs chr8 118371245 118371301 a1806613252 a3149920067 2 2

Assembly input: one row per pair, judged over the whole assembly.

Column Description chr, region_start, region_end the pair's region, from the catalog kmerA_id, kmerB_id the two uniqmer IDs kmerA_contig, kmerB_contig the first contig each uniqmer was found on kmerA_location, kmerB_location position of that hit on that contig (0-based) kmerA_hit_count, kmerB_hit_count total hits of each uniqmer across all contigs chr region_start region_end kmerA_id kmerB_id kmerA_contig kmerA_location kmerA_hit_count kmerB_contig kmerB_location kmerB_hit_count chr1 3074876 3074933 a482910377 a2918360054 h1tg000004l 3061207 3 h1tg000004l 3061327 3 chr8 118371245 118371301 a1806613252 a3149920067 h1tg000031l 9945112 1 h2tg000018l 4420571 4 chr17 44907520 44907571 a3308811109 a1274459938 h2tg000012l 21883540 2 h2tg000012l 21883640 1

docs.title: -d, --debug-file
docs.text:
One row per uniqmer pair in the catalog, saying whether it reached the main output and, if not, why.

Column Description kmerA_id, kmerB_id the two uniqmer IDs dropped yes if the pair is absent from the main output, else no reason why the pair was dropped, as a short phrase: one or both uniqmers not found, found too many times, never found together, or found on mismatched strands or in the wrong order. Empty when the pair was not dropped kmerA_id kmerB_id dropped reason a482910377 a2918360054 no a1806613252 a3149920067 yes kmer(s) hit more than once in a read a3308811109 a1274459938 yes kmers never found in the same read

docs.text:

docs.title: trumut allele
docs.text: A worked example on simulated data is under Quick start.

docs.title: Basic command
docs.text:
trumut allele [reads.bam] [catalog.tsv] [output.tsv] --input-type reads
trumut allele [assembly.fasta] [catalog.tsv] [output.tsv] --input-type assembly --ploidy [2]

  • input (reads.bam/assembly.fasta):

    • accepted types:

      • alignments (SAM, SAM.gz, BAM, CRAM)
      • assemblies (FASTA)
      • unaligned reads (FASTQ, FASTA, unaligned SAM/BAM)

    • can be given as local file, stdin, or a URL

  • [catalog.tsv]: uniqmer-annotated tandem repeat catalog from Pre-built files or trumut prep-catalog

  • [output.tsv]: output path
  • --input-type reads|assembly: reads for sequencing reads. assembly for assembled contigs
  • --ploidy N: required with assembly. Number of haplotype contigs per locus (e.g., 1 for a haploid assembly, 2 for diploid)

docs.title: For input
docs.text: Argument Default Description --input-fmt STR sniffed specify input file format -r, --reference FILE reference FASTA, needed for CRAM

docs.title: For output
docs.text: Argument Default Description --save-allele-seq off add an allele_seqs column: the read sequence between the two uniqmers --save-query-names off add a query_names column: read names, or contig names for assembly input --save-kmer-coords off add kmerA_ref_coords and kmerB_ref_coords columns: the reference-genome position of each uniqmer -w, --wrong-kmer-hits FILE none uniqmer pairs found in a read / contig on unexpected strands or in the wrong order. -m, --many-kmer-hits FILE none uniqmer pairs that were found more than once in a single read / contig -d, --debug-file FILE none one row per catalog uniqmer pair: whether it was dropped from the main output and, if so, why

docs.title: Indexed alignments
docs.text:
→ BAM, CRAM, or URL with a remote index

Argument Default Description -t, --target STR all process one chromosome only, spelled exactly as in the BAM/CRAM header -j, --jobs INT 3 number of chromosomes processed in parallel, one worker each; lowered automatically if that many would not fit in memory -q, --min-mapq INT 0 skip alignments below this MAPQ -@, --threads INT 3 threads passed to samtools for CRAM decoding, per worker

docs.title: Unindexed streams
docs.text:
→ SAM (aligned or not), unindexed BAM, stdin, FASTQ/FASTA reads

Argument Default Description -t, --target STR all SAM/BAM streams only: process one chromosome. chr1 and 1 both match -j, --jobs INT 3 scanning threads -q, --min-mapq INT 0 SAM/BAM streams only: skip alignments below this MAPQ -@, --threads INT 3 BGZF decompression threads for bgzip FASTQ or unaligned BAM

docs.title: Assemblies
docs.text:
→ FASTA contigs

Argument Default Description -t, --target STR all process one record (contig) only, by name -@, --threads INT 3 BGZF decompression threads for a bgzip assembly

docs.title: trumut cancer
docs.text: A worked example on simulated data is under Quick start.

docs.title: Basic command
docs.text:
trumut cancer [tumor.tsv] [normal.tsv] [output.tsv] --input-type reads
trumut cancer [tumor.tsv] [normal.tsv] [output.tsv] --input-type assembly --ploidy [2]
  • [tumor.tsv]: tumor output from trumut allele
  • [normal.tsv]: matched normal output from trumut allele
  • [output.tsv]: output path
  • --input-type reads|assembly: reads for sequencing reads. assembly for assembled contigs
  • --ploidy N: required with assembly. Number of haplotype contigs per locus (e.g., 1 for a haploid assembly, 2 for diploid)

docs.title: More options
docs.text: Argument Default Description -t chr1 all chromosomes process specified chromosome only, spelled as in the trumut allele output -j N 3 chromosomes processed in parallel --clustering-thres N 7 allele lengths within N bp of each other collapse into one reported allele --n-reads-thres N 9 a read supports an allele if its length is within N bp of it --min-offset N clustering width + 1 report a tumor allele only if it is at least N bp from every normal allele --min-supporting-reads N 7 report a tumor allele only if it has at least N supporting reads --min-motif-diff X 3 report a tumor allele only if its median motif k-mer count differs from the normal's by more than X --mega-events off report large events only. Sets --min-offset 100, --min-supporting-reads -1 unless given explicitly (--min-motif-diff stays 3) --min-reads-per-sample N 10; for assemblies, set by --ploidy skip a locus unless tumor and normal each have at least N reads / contigs there --min-subclone-reads N 4 call a tumor allele subclonal only if another allele or density peak on the same haplotype has at least N reads --min-subclone-frac F 0.1 that other allele or density peak must also hold at least this fraction of the haplotype's reads --min-tagged-frac F 0.5 use haplotype-aware event types only if at least this fraction of the locus's reads carry an HP tag --min-tagged-reads N 2 use haplotype-aware event types only if at least N HP-tagged reads support the allele --min-gap-kmers N 10 count a non-motif insertion toward n_nonmotif_kmers_in column value only if it holds at least N k-mers --min-gap-frac F 0.95 count a non-motif gap only if at least this fraction of its k-mers are newly inserted
